recommendation: Claim only two existing test files first. The maintained deployment operator already constructs the ordinary SDK node under the CLI exact-endpoint authentication wrapper and passes that same object to PXE. Establish actual compatibility before proposing any production client change.
supersedes: The conditional broader candidateFutureClientClaim in client-coverage-readonly.json is not needed for the maintained deployment operator based on this call graph. No change to trusted-private-node or public wallet credential boundaries is proposed.

callGraph.fact: CLI installs createCliRpcFetch before loading the SDK bundle, evaluates .build/sdk/aztec_bundle.js, and supplies openPXEStore. Module top-level parses manifests; importing the whole CLI would invoke unrelated setup.

rawNode is a.createAztecNodeClient(config.aztecNodeUrl); ordinary preflight uses it; aztecNode=rawNode is passed into a.createPXE with the real application store. No createTrustedPrivateNode call is used.

Application wrapper accepts this node directly, forwards to actual lazy SDK PXE, records its opaque cached node, and provides an existing readOnly option that skips application prover initialization and rejects proveTx.

Actual PXE reads NodeInfo and genesis, wraps input in withCache, starts its operation queue and registers protocol/preloaded contracts; stop drains queue/synchronizer and closes store. This is real initialization, potentially substantive hashing work, not a fake PXE or necessarily a cheap import.
Credential-free private facade uses omit/no-referrer and intentionally bypasses CLI injection. It is a separate public-app privacy boundary, not the maintained deployment operator route.
